context: A uni student debates a teacher about civic discourse
purpose: Teach: 公明党/火星/追悼/後退/帰還/露出/断言/賭け

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 先生、最近の政治って一歩後退してませんか。市民の声が全然届いてない気がするんです。
lines.en: Professor, isn't recent politics taking a step backward? I feel like citizens' voices aren't reaching them at all.
lines.style: Frustrated student opening a serious debate respectfully

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: そう断言するのは早いわよ。例えば公明党の連立への姿勢ひとつ取っても、議論は動いている。
lines.en: It's too early to declare that. Take Komeito's stance on the coalition alone—debate is actually moving.
lines.style: Calm teacher pushing back with measured authority

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: でもメディアでの露出ばかり増えて、中身の議論は浅いままじゃないですか。
lines.en: But media exposure just keeps increasing while the substance of debate stays shallow, doesn't it?
lines.style: Sharper challenge from engaged young voter

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: それは有権者側の責任でもある。先月の追悼式での首相演説、ちゃんと最後まで聞いた人がどれだけいた？
lines.en: That's partly the voters' responsibility too. How many actually listened to the PM's speech at last month's memorial ceremony?
lines.style: Teacher redirecting blame to civic apathy firmly

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 正直、聞いてません。でも僕らの世代は、火星に人を送る話より目の前の家賃が気になるんですよ。
lines.en: Honestly, I didn't. But our generation cares more about rent than sending people to Mars.
lines.style: Candid admission shifting to generational economic concerns

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 気持ちは分かる。けれど宇宙から無事帰還した飛行士の言葉一つで、若者の関心が変わることもある。
lines.en: I understand the feeling. But a single word from an astronaut safely returned from space can shift young people's interest.
lines.style: Veteran educator offering reflective counterexample, voice clear and distinctly their own

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: つまり、政治に人生を賭けて関わる価値はある、と？
lines.en: So you're saying it's worth betting your life on political engagement?
lines.style: Probing question, testing teacher's true position

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 賭けるかどうかはあなた次第。ただ、無関心が一番危ない、それだけは覚えておきなさい。
lines.en: Whether you bet is up to you. Just remember—indifference is the most dangerous thing of all.
lines.style: Closing line, firm parting wisdom from mentor
